note: Any post-seal canonical or route failure is retained externally and does not rewrite this repository file.

rows.failure: The first multi-command precommit inspection wrapper contained an unmatched JavaScript delimiter and failed before launching any shell command.
rows.recovery: Split the inspection into separate bounded read-only calls, retain this wrapper failure, and do not replay the successful planning build.

rows.failure: The first non-sparse Git add rejected every new planning path outside the existing sparse definition; the empty staged-set comparison then emitted a nonterminating null-list error before printing an invalid success label.
rows.recovery: Use Git add with the explicit sparse option, set PowerShell errors to terminating, require a nonempty staged set, and compare it exactly with the committed allowlist.

rows.failure: The first x1 session reached the first local-runner smoke after its in-memory contract checks, then Node rejected the generated runner because the Python f-string emitted a literal line break inside a JavaScript string.
rows.recovery: Correct only the runner newline escaping, preserve this exact failed receipt, and resume the failed x1 session; no successful session is replayed.

rows.failure: Node --check rejected both TXT entrypoints with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION before it could inspect their syntax.
rows.recovery: Use the same Node CommonJS main execution and Module._compile loader that the TXT interfaces declare, then inspect captured stderr from the exact runner.

rows.failure: The committed x2 skill-validation receipt stored five installed-skill path labels under the raw local user-profile prefix.
rows.recovery: Retain the exact x2 commit and original blob hash, then replace only the five final-tree path labels with %CODEX_HOME% in the additive final correction delta; do not replay x2.

rows.failure: The first final build stopped at its bounded privacy scan because the phone-like detector accepted digit runs inside Git hashes and a DOI as candidates.
rows.recovery: Require non-alphanumeric boundaries and an explicit plus or grouped separator signal, retain the failed final attempt, and continue only the unsealed final dependency without rerunning x1 or x2.

rows.failure: The first isolated regex diagnostic over-escaped backslashes and incorrectly reported zero matches.
rows.recovery: Use the detector's exact compiled pattern and print the matched substrings; nine false-positive numeric fragments were then identified.

rows.failure: The first final-resume privacy dependency still used the stale detector expression and classified the DOI as phone-like in seven owner files; the preceding standalone expression had not been synchronized into the generator.
rows.recovery: Use one file-backed compiled detector, synchronize the exact expression into the generator, exclude path and DOI suffix contexts, and require positive plus negative controls.

rows.failure: The first file-backed DOI-safe phone detector returned zero repository candidates but rejected the declared parenthesized phone-format positive control.
rows.recovery: Separate plus-prefixed, parenthesized-area-code, and hyphen-or-space-grouped alternatives while retaining DOI, hash, and phase-label negative controls.

rows.failure: The next final-resume privacy scan correctly found that the literal synthetic parenthesized phone control had been copied into two public failure records.
rows.recovery: Retain the exact literal only in the private D-first failure receipt and replace the public value with a semantic phone-format label before rescanning.
